If your embroidery thread keeps breaking and the broken area looks fuzzy, frayed, or damaged, the problem may not be thread tension. In many cases, the cause is an incorrectly installed needle or incorrect needle direction. author: Kimi Embroidery Repair Tech Station
SymptomsYou may notice one or more of the following:
The upper thread breaks repeatedly during embroidery. The thread break point looks fuzzy or worn out. The thread appears to be cut or scraped instead of cleanly broken. The same needle position keeps causing thread breaks. Adjusting thread tension does not solve the problem. Thread break caused by incorrect needle directionCommon CausesThe most common causes include:
The needle is installed in the wrong direction. The needle is not fully inserted into the needle bar. The needle is bent or damaged. The needle eye has a sharp edge or burr. The thread is rubbing against the needle incorrectly during high-speed embroidery. Why Incorrect Needle Direction Causes Thread BreaksAn embroidery needle is designed with a specific front and back direction.
Correct needle directionCorrect needle direction（back）Correct needle direction（frontcmdgit add .git commit -m "更新内容"git push origin main）When the needle is installed incorrectly:
The thread cannot pass smoothly through the needle eye. The thread rubs against the edge of the needle eye. High-speed movement creates excessive friction. The thread fibers become damaged before breaking. This is why the broken thread often appears:
Fuzzy Frayed Split into multiple fibers Similar to being cut by a sharp edge Step 1 — Check the Needle InstallationBefore adjusting tension or replacing other parts:
Turn off the machine. Remove the needle. Install a new needle correctly. Make sure the needle is fully inserted. Confirm the needle direction matches the machine requirements. A needle that is slightly rotated or installed backward can cause continuous thread breaks.
Step 2 — Inspect the Needle ConditionCheck for:
A bent needle tip. A damaged needle eye. Scratches or burrs on the needle. Signs of thread rubbing. Even a small defect on the needle can damage embroidery thread.
Step 3 — Check the Thread PathAfter confirming the needle direction, inspect:
Thread passing through all guides correctly. Thread entering the tension discs properly. Thread not catching on any sharp edges. Thread break sensor area for excessive friction. Step 4 — Test the MachineAfter installing a correct needle:
Thread the machine again. Run a test embroidery design. Observe whether the thread break continues. Compare the broken thread condition. If the thread is no longer frayed, the issue was caused by needle installation or needle damage.
If the Thread Still BreaksIf the problem continues after replacing and installing the needle correctly, check:
Upper thread tension. Bobbin tension. Bobbin case condition. Rotary hook damage. Design density and embroidery speed. Thread quality and compatibility. Preventive MaintenanceTo reduce thread break problems:
Replace needles regularly. Always install needles in the correct direction. Do not continue using damaged or bent needles. Clean the hook area and remove lint regularly. Use the correct needle size for the fabric and thread type. SummaryWhen embroidery thread breaks and the break point looks frayed or fuzzy, do not immediately adjust the tension.
First check the needle direction and needle condition.
A correctly installed needle allows the thread to pass smoothly through the needle eye, reducing friction and preventing unnecessary thread damage.
Troubleshooting order: Check needle direction → Replace damaged needle → Check thread path → Adjust tension if needed.
Need More Help?If the thread continues breaking after checking the needle, record a short video showing:
The needle installation direction. The thread path. The broken thread area. The embroidery process. This information will help diagnose the problem more accurately.

If your machine displays Error! [10000001] info(00000000), the main shaft is unable to return to its home position (100°). In most cases, the problem is caused by a mechanical jam rather than an electronic failure.
SymptomsYou may notice one or more of the following:
The machine stops during startup.
The main shaft cannot return to 100°.
The handwheel is difficult or impossible to turn.
The machine displays:
main shaft starts error!Error! [10000001] info(00000000) Common CausesThe most common causes include:
Thread or lint jammed inside the bobbin area. The bobbin case is installed incorrectly. A broken needle is stuck in the hook. Thread wrapped around the rotary hook. The machine was powered off during embroidery, causing the shaft position to become incorrect. Step 1 — Turn Off the MachineBefore performing any inspection:
Turn off the machine. Disconnect the power. Remove the embroidery hoop if installed. Step 2 — Inspect the Bobbin AreaRemove the bobbin and bobbin case.
Check for:
Tangled thread Fabric debris Broken needle fragments Lint buildup Clean the hook thoroughly before reinstalling the bobbin case.
Tip: Simply adding oil will not solve a mechanical jam. Always clean the hook area first.
Step 3 — Check the Main ShaftSlowly rotate the handwheel by hand.
It should rotate smoothly. If it feels tight or becomes stuck, do not force it. Reinspect the hook area for anything blocking movement. Step 4 — Restart the MachineAfter cleaning:
Reinstall the bobbin case correctly. Turn the machine back on. Allow the machine to perform its automatic initialization. If the shaft returns to 100°, the error should disappear.
If the Error RemainsIf the machine still reports:
Error! [10000001] info(00000000) Check for:
Damaged rotary hook Bent needle bar Timing issues Main shaft obstruction Sensor or encoder problems These issues may require professional inspection.
Video TutorialWatch the complete troubleshooting process for the Main Shaft Error.
This video demonstrates how to troubleshoot and fix the Main Shaft Error (Error! [10000001] info(00000000)). Follow each step carefully before disassembling any machine components. If the problem persists after following the steps in this video, contact Kimi Embroidery Repair Tech Station for further assistance.
Preventive MaintenanceTo reduce the chance of this error:
Clean the hook area every day. Remove thread buildup after each project. Replace bent or damaged needles immediately. Oil the machine according to the maintenance schedule. Never force the handwheel when resistance is present. Need More Help?If the problem continues after cleaning the hook and reinstalling the bobbin case, record a short video showing:
The error screen The bobbin area The handwheel turning by hand This will help us diagnose the problem more accurately.

How to Adjust Belt TensionThe belt system plays an important role in controlling the movement of the embroidery frame and machine components.
Over time, belts may become loose due to long-term operation, temperature changes, or normal wear. Incorrect belt tension can affect embroidery accuracy and machine performance.
When Should You Adjust Belt Tension?Belt tension adjustment may be needed when you notice:
Abnormal noise during machine operation
Loose or improperly tensioned belts may create unusual sounds while the machine is running.
Embroidery design position shifting
Incorrect belt tension can cause the hoop movement to become inaccurate, resulting in design misalignment.
Visible belt looseness
A belt that has noticeable slack may require adjustment.
Long-term machine use maintenance
Periodic belt inspection helps maintain stable machine performance.
Symptoms of Incorrect Belt TensionBelt Too LooseA loose belt may cause:
Embroidery pattern displacement Poor positioning accuracy Delayed or uneven movement Increased operating noise Belt Too TightAn overly tight belt may cause:
Increased motor load Abnormal mechanical noise Faster belt wear Reduced machine movement smoothness Proper belt tension allows the machine to move smoothly while maintaining accurate embroidery positioning.
How to Adjust Belt TensionFollow these steps to check and adjust belt tension:
Step 1: Turn Off the MachineTurn off the embroidery machine. Disconnect the power supply. Move the embroidery arm or hoop carefully to access the belt area. Step 2: Check the Belt ConditionInspect the belt:
Check for visible looseness. Check whether the belt has excessive vibration during operation. Check for signs of wear or damage. Step 3: Adjust Belt TensionLocate the belt tension adjustment mechanism. Loosen the fixing screws slightly. Adjust the tension until the belt has proper resistance. Tighten the screws securely after adjustment. Do not over-tighten the belt. The belt should be firm but still allow smooth movement.
Step 4: Test the MachineAfter adjustment:
Turn on the machine. Run a test movement or embroidery design. Check: Movement noise Hoop positioning accuracy Embroidery alignment Fine adjustments may be required depending on machine usage and belt condition.
Maintenance TipsCheck belt tension regularly as part of machine maintenance. Avoid adjusting belt tension without confirming the actual cause of the issue. If the belt is damaged, replace it instead of only adjusting tension. After adjustment, always test embroidery accuracy. Computer Cannot Detect the SmartStitch Machine — Check SettingsOne of the most frustrating issues in digital embroidery is when your computer simply does not recognise the SmartStitch machine. This prevents design transfer, parameter adjustments, and real‑time monitoring.
Most detection failures are not hardware‑related – they originate from incorrect settings, driver conflicts, or cable/port issues. Follow this structured troubleshooting process to quickly isolate and fix the problem.
Common Root CausesMachine not powered on or in the wrong mode (e.g., offline / manual) Faulty or loose USB/serial cable Incorrect COM port or baud rate settings in the software Outdated or missing USB drivers Firewall or antivirus blocking the communication port Multiple software instances accessing the same port Damaged port on the computer or on the machine Step‑by‑Step Diagnostic ProcessPerform these checks in the recommended order – from the simplest to the most advanced.
Step 1: Verify Power and Machine StatusEnsure the SmartStitch machine is turned on and the display shows online or ready mode. If the machine has a “PC Link” or “Remote” button, press it to enable communication. Step 2: Check the Physical CableInspect the USB or serial cable for visible damage (kinks, cuts, bent pins). Try a different cable that is known to work (even a short one). Reconnect both ends firmly; listen for a click on USB‑type connectors. Step 3: Restart and Re‑detectRestart both the machine and the computer. Unplug the cable, wait 10 seconds, then plug it back in while the software is open. Watch for the system tray notification that a new device is connected. Step 4: Check Driver Installation (Windows)Open Device Manager and expand “Ports (COM & LPT)” or “Universal Serial Bus controllers”. Look for “SmartStitch” or an unrecognised device with a yellow exclamation mark. If missing, install or re‑install the driver provided with the machine (or download from the manufacturer’s site). For Mac/Linux, check system information for USB device listing. Step 5: Verify COM Port and Baud Rate in the SoftwareOpen the SmartStitch communication settings (usually under Settings > Machine Connection). Ensure the selected COM port matches the one assigned in Device Manager. Set the baud rate to the value recommended for your model (commonly 115200 or 9600). Important: If you have multiple COM ports, select the one that appears when the cable is plugged in. Step 6: Close Conflicting ApplicationsClose any other embroidery software or serial monitor tools that may be holding the same port. Restart the SmartStitch software alone and try detection again. Step 7: Disable Firewall / Antivirus TemporarilySome security software blocks virtual COM ports. Temporarily disable them (remember to re‑enable later) and test. Step 8: Test with Another ComputerIf available, connect the machine to a different PC. If it detects successfully, the issue lies with your original computer’s settings or USB port. Quick Reference Decision TableSymptom Primary Check Secondary Check No reaction at all when connecting Cable & power (Step 1‑2) USB port hardware Device appears but software says “not found” COM port / baud rate (Step 5) Driver (Step 4) Detection works sporadically Cable replacement Interference / grounding Error “port already in use” Close other apps (Step 6) Restart PC Preventive MeasuresAlways use the original cable supplied with the machine. Keep a spare cable and a separate driver installer on a USB stick. Label the COM port used so you don’t accidentally change it. Perform a connection test before starting a large production batch. Update the SmartStitch software to the latest version regularly. How to Fix Bobbin Thread Showing on Top of EmbroideryThe upper thread tension is too tight compared to the bobbin tension, which is why the bobbin thread is being pulled to the top. Please reduce the upper thread tension or increase the bobbin tension to balance them.
When the bobbin thread appears on the top side of an embroidery design, it usually means the thread tension balance is incorrect.
In a properly balanced embroidery stitch, the bobbin thread should remain hidden on the back side of the design, while the upper thread should cover the visible embroidery area.
SymptomsYou may notice:
White or bobbin-colored thread appearing on the top of the design. Small dots or lines of bobbin thread visible in the embroidery. Poor stitch appearance even though the design is aligned correctly. The upper thread does not fully cover the embroidery area. Common CausesThe most common causes include:
Upper thread tension is too tight. Bobbin tension is too loose. Incorrect bobbin installation. Wrong needle size or damaged needle. Incorrect thread type or thread weight. Poor stabilization of the fabric. Design density or digitizing issues. Step 1 — Check Upper Thread TensionIf the upper thread tension is too tight, it can pull the bobbin thread to the front.
Check:
Reduce the upper thread tension gradually. Run a test embroidery. Compare the front and back sides of the design. Avoid making large tension adjustments at once.
Step 2 — Check Bobbin Installation and TensionRemove the bobbin case and check:
The bobbin is installed in the correct direction. The bobbin thread passes correctly through the tension spring. The bobbin case is clean and free of lint. If the bobbin tension is too loose, the bobbin thread may be pulled to the top.
Step 3 — Check Needle and Thread SelectionIncorrect needle or thread combinations can affect stitch balance.
Check:
Use the correct needle size for the thread. Replace bent or damaged needles. Confirm the thread is suitable for embroidery. Step 4 — Check Stabilizer and Fabric SupportInsufficient stabilization can cause the fabric to move and affect thread tension.
Make sure:
The correct stabilizer is used. The fabric is firmly hooped. The material does not move during embroidery. Step 5 — Check Design SettingsSome designs may naturally require adjustment.
Check:
Stitch density. Underlay settings. Pull compensation. Small lettering settings. A poorly digitized design can also cause tension imbalance.
Test After AdjustmentAfter making adjustments:
Run a small test design. Check the front and back sides. Confirm the bobbin thread is mostly visible only on the back. Continue adjusting until the stitch balance is correct. Preventive MaintenanceTo reduce the chance of bobbin thread showing on top:

How to Replace the Thread Break SensorThe Thread Break Sensor is an important part of the embroidery machine’s thread detection system. It monitors the movement of the upper thread and helps the machine detect when the thread has broken, run out, or is not feeding correctly.
When the sensor detects a thread break, the machine can stop embroidery and alert the operator so the problem can be corrected before continuing.
What Does the Thread Break Sensor Do?The Thread Break Sensor monitors the upper thread during embroidery.
Its main functions include:
Detecting when the upper thread breaks Detecting when the thread runs out Monitoring thread movement during stitching Stopping the machine when a thread-break condition is detected Helping prevent the machine from continuing to stitch without thread Symptoms of a Thread Break Sensor ProblemA faulty or incorrectly installed sensor may cause symptoms such as:
The machine does not detect a thread break. The machine stops even though the thread is intact. The machine repeatedly reports a thread-break error. The sensor does not respond correctly to thread movement. The machine continues stitching after the upper thread has broken. Before replacing the sensor, check that the thread is routed correctly and that there is no dust, lint, or debris interfering with the sensor.
How to Replace the Thread Break SensorIf the Thread Break Sensor is confirmed to be faulty, it may need to be replaced.
Follow the replacement procedure shown in the video below.
Video TutorialThe following video demonstrates how to remove the old Thread Break Sensor and install the replacement.
Important NoteAfter replacing the sensor, make sure it is installed in the correct position and that the thread passes through the sensor correctly.
Test the machine after installation to confirm that the sensor can correctly detect thread movement and thread breaks.
If the problem continues after replacing the sensor, check the thread path, sensor wiring, connector, and related machine settings.

SmartStitch System Update — Full Uncut WalkthroughProblemA SmartStitch embroidery machine may require a system update to improve performance, fix software issues, or support new features.
However, an incorrect or incomplete update can cause communication errors, version mismatches, or machine operation problems.
This guide explains the complete SmartStitch system update process from start to finish.
SymptomsAfter an incorrect update, users may experience:
The update failed because the system version is outdated. Common error examples:
“The M4 Does Not Match EMB Version” CAN communication errors System version mismatch Possible CausesCommon causes of update problems include:
System update fails during installation. The machine model and the update file model do not match. The versions are different. The file has not been extracted yet. The program is placed inside a folder on the USB drive, which is incorrect ❌ Please put the program files directly in the USB drive (root directory) instead ✅ How to CheckBefore updating:
Confirm the exact machine model. Check the current system version. Confirm the update file matches the machine model. Use a reliable USB drive.(It is recommended to use a USB drive smaller than 32GB.) Make sure the machine has stable power. After updating:
Check the new system version. Confirm the machine starts normally. Test needle movement. Test color change. Test thread trimming. Run a small embroidery test. SolutionFollow the update procedure carefully:
Step 1: Prepare the Update FileDownload the correct update package. Extract the update file first, then copy the extracted program files to the USB drive. The key step is to extract (unzip) the file first. Do not rename or modify the update files unless instructed. Step 2: Start the UpdateTurn on the machine. Insert the USB drive. Follow the update instructions on the screen. Wait until the update is completely finished. Do not:
Turn off the machine during updating. Remove the USB drive during updating. Press unnecessary buttons during the update process. Step 3: Verify the UpdateAfter the update is complete:
Confirm the software version. Restart the machine. Check all major functions. Important NoteA system update should only be performed with the correct update file for your exact SmartStitch model.
Using the wrong version may cause system compatibility problems.

How to Adjust Thread Trimming ParametersProper thread trimming settings are important for maintaining embroidery quality and ensuring stable stitching after color changes or trims.
Incorrect trimming parameters may cause the following issues:
Thread tail too short after trimming
The remaining thread tail is not long enough, causing the upper thread to easily pull out of the needle when embroidery starts again.
Thread tail too long after trimming
Excess thread remains on the back of the embroidery, creating loose thread tails and affecting the finished appearance.
Frequent thread trimming during small lettering or detailed embroidery
Incorrect trimming settings may cause thread breaks, missed stitches, or unstable starting stitches after trimming.
Adjusting the thread trimming parameters can help improve embroidery consistency and reduce unnecessary thread problems.
When Should You Adjust Thread Trimming Parameters?You may need to adjust the trimming parameters when:
The upper thread comes out of the needle after trimming. The thread tail left after trimming is too short or too long. Small letters or detailed designs frequently have starting stitch problems. The back side of the embroidery has excessive loose thread tails. How to Adjust Thread Trimming ParametersFollow these steps to adjust the thread trimming settings:
Step 1: Open Machine SettingsTurn on the embroidery machine. Enter the Settings menu. Find the Embroidery Parameters option. Locate the Thread Trimming Parameters settings. Step 2: Adjust the Thread Tail LengthAdjust the trimming parameter according to the embroidery result:
If the thread tail is too short:
Increase the trimming thread length value. Leave enough upper thread after trimming to ensure the needle can catch the thread properly when restarting. If the thread tail is too long:
Decrease the trimming thread length value. Reduce excess thread remaining on the back of the embroidery. Step 3: Test the Embroidery ResultAfter adjusting:
Run a test embroidery design. Check the starting stitches after trimming. Inspect the back side of the embroidery. Fine-tune the value if necessary. Small adjustments may be needed depending on:
Thread type and brand Fabric thickness Design density Embroidery speed Tips for Better Thread Trimming PerformanceAvoid setting the trimming thread length too short, as it may cause frequent needle unthreading. Avoid setting it too long, as excess thread can affect embroidery appearance. For small lettering and detailed designs, proper trimming settings help maintain clean starts and reduce thread breaks. Always test adjustments with the same fabric and thread combination used for production. Welcome!Welcome to the Docsy theme user guide! This guide shows you how to get started creating technical documentation sites using Docsy, including site customization and how to use Docsy’s blocks and templates.
What is Docsy?Docsy is a theme for the Hugo static site generator that’s specifically designed for technical documentation sets and has a lot of best practices built in. Use Docsy to get a working and reliable documentation site up and running fast, and then get back to focusing on great content for your users. Learn more about Docsy.
